expectations.text: Lists six cans: tithe, finish free, educate, save, have fun, pay bills
expectations.evidence: Cans are 'Giving / Tithe', 'Savings', 'Investing', 'Education', 'Business reinvestment / Opportunity', 'Living'. No 'finish free' or 'have fun' can; 'Business reinvestment' is invented. Response admits 'I can't confirm his exact can names or percentages'.

expectations.text: Uses the percentages (10/10/10/10/10/50 or as stated)
expectations.evidence: Numbers are 10/10/10/10/10/50, but they are attached to invented cans (e.g. 10% to 'Business reinvestment') and presented as 'a reasonable example'; it also offers an alternate 10/15/25/15/25/10 split. The book's percentages are not applied to the book's cans.

expectations.text: Applies them to $500 with dollar amounts
expectations.evidence: Table gives $50 x5 and $250, totaling $500, arithmetic correct.

Purposes describe its own cans, not Golden's: no 'have fun' can that must be spent monthly (fun folded into 'Living'); finish-free's rule only partly echoed under 'Investing'; 'Business reinvestment' purpose is invented. The quote-like claim 'a person who can't give $50 out of $500 won't give $5,000...' is not in SKILL.md.

expectations.text: Mentions a mental trap or 'you are in the marketing business'
expectations.evidence: No money trap is named and the 'you are in the marketing business' principle is absent; only a generic 'especially in sales, marketing and offers' under Education.
